subject: RadixHealth: Competitive deep-dive, decision criteria & follow-up tests
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@radixhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena@radixhealth.com>, Product Team <product@radixhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — quick notes

Camila — thanks again for the demo earlier. High level reaction from our side: we like Redwood's approach to consistent latency and the deployment flexibility (esp. private VPC). Two things we need to be confident on before moving this forward to procurement:

1) Performance parity across bursty traffic vs. steady loads — our scheduling spikes are very concentrated around 9–11am PT.
2) Small-model accuracy drift when using 4-bit / q4 quantized variants — our clinicians flagged hallucination risk on edge cases.

Can you and your team run a short side-by-side that focuses on those two items? If you can also include a simple cost projection for 3 and 12 month horizons that would help the execs.

Thanks — Sanjay
Sanjay Rao | Head of Engineering, RadixHealth


From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@radixhealth.com>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena@radixhealth.com>, Product Team <product@radixhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — quick notes

Sanjay — really appreciate the clear asks. Quick recap from our side of what we heard (so we don't miss anything):

- Primary goals: keep clinician latency under 250ms p50 during morning spikes; retain hallucination/accuracy parity within existing QA thresholds when using quantized model variants.
- Acceptance criteria: latency p50 < 250ms and <1% regression on the clinical QA prompt set (we discussed the 120 prompts you shared).
- Constraints: Radix requires private deployment (VPC) for PHI, SOC2 + quarterly penetration testing for vendor selection — thanks for flagging that.

Proposed quick plan (we can run this as a 72-hour sprint):
1) Performance burst test: simulate 2x and 5x concurrent user load for the 9–11am window on a dedicated pool; measure p50/p95 and tail latency. Owner: Marissa.
2) Quantization parity test: run the 120 clinical prompts across the floated full-precision model and the q4/q8 variants; diff outputs, and compute F1 + hallucination flagging metric. Owner: Karthik.
3) Cost projection: run simple throughput-based cost model for steady vs. burst profiles and provide monthly vs. annual options. Owner: Camila.

Attachments: I attached a short interop test spec (interop-test-specs.xlsx) and a redlined high-level proposal (redwood-proposal-diff.pdf).

Next steps: if that plan looks right, Marissa will reach out to set a time to run the first load test (we'll need a small set of performance keys and a short network checklist for VPC onboarding). Can you confirm 72 hours is sufficient?

Best —
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@radixhealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Elena Martinez <elena@radixhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — quick notes

Sanjay / Elena — looping in the operational owner for the burst tests. Quick operational notes and an ask for Radix: 

- I'll provision a dedicated test pool in our staging Dedicated environment. We'll push synthetic traffic that mirrors your usage shape (targeted 9–11am window).
- Network checklist for VPC peering (we'll need these from Radix): 1) CIDR ranges for peering, 2) a test NAT host/public egress IP for our load generator, 3) any firewall rules that might block long-lived TLS connections.
- For the test keys: we'll generate short-lived performance keys scoped to the test pool — safe for sharing to your test team.

Open questions we should resolve before kicking off:
- Is the 120 clinical prompt set final, or should we expect an updated set from your QA team?
- For hallucination definition: do you have an internal process/label that we should use, or should we use Redwood's heuristic (we'll mark outputs with our hallucination scorer and then have Radix QA review a sample)?

I'll tentatively schedule the burst test for Monday 24 Aug 2026 09:00–12:00 PT unless you suggest otherwise. If Monday doesn't work, please propose two alternative half-day windows.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Ops Lead | Redwood Inference
Attachment: interop-test-specs.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Elena Martinez <elena@radixhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@radixhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — quick notes

Thanks team — the plan looks good. A few quick clarifications from Radix QA: 

- The 120 prompt set is final for this sprint; we'll only add edge cases if the initial run surfaces large gaps.
- For hallucination labeling: we'll apply Radix's internal label set (binary: "confident" vs "needs review") for the sample review. If Redwood can provide the hallucination scorer as a CSV of confidence scores + flagged spans, that will speed our review.
- Monday 24 Aug 09:00–12:00 PT works for the load window. Please send the test keys and network checklist by EOD Monday 23 Aug.

Also one ask from procurement: can you share an editable version of the redlined proposal so we can track local redlines?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Elena
Elena Martinez | Director of Product, RadixHealth
